chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
What the snare seizes and cuts off something from it — that part is dead (maytah). But what you find of the rest of its body still alive — slaughter it, then eat from it.

key_terms.الحبالة: al-hibalah — the snare, trap, or net used for hunting; the word derives from habala (rope/cord)
key_terms.ذكّه: dhakkahu — perform tadhkiya on it, i.e., execute the ritual slaughter (dhabh) with the prescribed incantation, making the meat halal
key_terms.ميت: maytah — carrion, an animal that has died without lawful ritual slaughter; categorically forbidden to consume

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on eating game caught in a snare or trap according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules on game caught in a snare: any portion severed by the trap before the hunter arrives is considered carrion (maytah) and therefore haram, since it died without ritual slaughter. However, if the hunter reaches the animal and finds any portion of the body still alive, it is obligatory to perform tadhkiya (ritual slaughter) on that living portion, after which it becomes permissible to eat. This ruling reflects the fundamental Islamic principle that meat is only lawful if proper ritual slaughter has been performed on a living animal.
